candidates.description: AI agent security scanner. Detect vulnerabilities in agent configurations, MCP servers, and tool permissions. Available as CLI, GitHub Action, ECC plugin, and GitHub App integration. 🛡️
candidates.why: Agent-config auditor (.claude secrets, broad permissions, risky hooks, MCP) with grade/SARIF; the plugin's check-agent-config plus AGT-1/AGT-3/AGT-5/AGT-9 already cover it. Unpinned npx and @v1 action (NPM-1/SEC-17); optional --opus/OrcaRouter modes send configs to hosted models (AGT-4); runtime install adds a PreToolUse hook.

candidates.description: Open detection-rule standard for AI agent security threats — like Sigma, but for AI agents. Executable, testable rules for prompt injection, tool poisoning, context exfiltration and MCP attacks. Merge
candidates.why: A Sigma-style YAML rule format, with test cases, for prompt injection, tool poisoning and skill compromise. atr scan checks SKILL.md files and MCP configs and emits SARIF. It overlaps AGT-5's pinned skill scanner, which the README says already consumes ATR rules. Draft spec (v4.1.5) with a single maintainer whose company sells products built on it; rule counts are inconsistent and false-positive rates were withdrawn pending re-measurement.

Protect against malicious code installed via npm, yarn, pnpm, npx, pnpx, pip, uv and poetry with Aikido Safe Chain. Free to use, no tokens required.

candidates.description: CLI tool and library for generating a Software Bill of Materials from container images and filesystems
candidates.why: SBOM generator already named by SEC-16/CFG-3 (syft per release in client mode); nothing new for the standard.

candidates.description: A lightweight sandboxing tool for enforcing filesystem and network restrictions on arbitrary processes at the OS level, without requiring a container.
candidates.why: Extends the AGT-2 sandbox (Claude Code only today) to headless, CI and non-Claude agents (AGT-6). Pre-1.0 (v0.0.83), 325 open issues, one low network-escape advisory GHSA-9gqj-5w7c-vx47.

candidates.description: Runtime security for AI apps and agents: prompt injection detection, tool-call authorization, sensitive-data redaction, bot protection, and rate limiting. Drop it into your JS/TS code.
candidates.why: Vendor SDK for app-level prompt-injection detection, tool-call authorization and redaction. AGT-4 deliberately requires removing a trifecta leg rather than relying on detection, and AI-4/AI-6/SEC-19 cover limits and confirmations. It needs an Arcjet cloud key.

candidates.description: The independent security agent for AI-written software. Finds issues, investigates whether they are real, and shows you the evidence. Deterministic core, no API key needed, JSON and SARIF output.
Catch dangerous AI agent skills before they catch you. Zero-dependency security scanner for Agent Skills, SKILL.md and MCP configs.
candidates.why: Zero-dependency static scanner for SKILL.md, agent instructions and MCP configs (14 heuristic rules, SARIF, --fail-on high). AGT-5 already requires a pinned static skill scanner at intake (cisco-ai-skill-scanner, with NVIDIA SkillSpector as the alternative), and both are pinned sources, so this duplicates them. Self-reported benchmark is 48 synthetic fixtures. Install is git clone of the default branch, and the Action is a mutable tag @v0.2.1, not a SHA (SEC-17). Single maintainer. Read from the README only.

candidates.description: Find leaked secrets everywhere.
candidates.why: Secrets scanner by gitleaks' original author; the standard already runs gitleaks everywhere (CI, pre-commit, AI-5). Watch as a possible gitleaks successor (LIFE-1) — live validation (-v/-a) calls providers, so default scans only.

candidates.description: poutine, a supply chain vulnerability scanner for build pipelines
candidates.why: CI pipeline misconfiguration scanner (GitHub, GitLab, Azure, Tekton; SARIF). For GitHub Actions zizmor (SEC-17) and std.workflows semgrep already cover it; adds only non-GitHub CI. Version-check telemetry on by default.

candidates.description: Agentic SDLC infrastructure. Define guardrails. Collect signals. Enforce continuously. Signed records of what your AI coding agents and CI/CD pipelines did, checked against policies as code, with the
candidates.why: Signed in-toto records of agent sessions and CI, with Rego policy gates. Partly overlaps AGT-10 (OTel audit of agent sessions) and SEC-32/SUP-4/SUP-7 attestations. A requireTrace push gate is new, but it installs git and agent hooks via a curl|bash installer and is a platform, not a rule.

candidates.description: Scan MCP servers for potential threats & security findings.
candidates.why: Scans MCP server tool descriptions, prompts and configs (YARA offline; static mode reads pre-generated JSON), which would give AGT-5's manual re-review of tool descriptions a mechanical check. It comes from the vendor of the already-pinned skill-scanner. Partial overlap: AGT-5 already mandates pinning and re-review, the README documents no description pinning or diff (rug-pull) feature, and its LLM, Cisco AI Defense and VirusTotal analyzers send data off-box, so an amendment would require YARA-only (AGT-4).

candidates.description: Security Scanner for Agent Skills
candidates.why: Mechanical skill scanning (YARA-X, AST and dataflow, SARIF, CI action) for AGT-5 intake beyond the consume fetch heuristics. Concern: use-llm mode sends skill text to an LLM provider; static-only or local model required. LICENSE is the Apache-2.0 short notice.

candidates.description: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings
warnings: G5: 486.5 stars/day — over the limit, vendor-exempt: verify the vendor really publishes it
candidates.why: Audit method: coverage record, adversarial disproval of each finding, confirmed / needs_validation / rejected plus JSON schema; strengthens APP_REVIEW finding discipline and AGT-13. Flag: 71.9k stars in 5 months with 3 contributors (vendor-exempt) so verify provenance at consume.

candidates.description: Give the agent a machine. Just not yours. Each AI coding agent gets its own isolated machine with root, Docker, and systemd - active defense detects and stops threats automatically.
candidates.why: Incus-container isolation with nftables egress allow-list for agent CLIs; AGT-2 and the pinned sandbox-runtime source already require OS-level sandboxing with a network allow-list. Install is curl|bash from master (unpinned, SUP-1/AGT-5).

candidates.description: Tamper-evident tracing, policy gates and cross-checks for AI agents: see what the agent did, and why.
candidates.why: Signed, hash-chained tool-call records with argument-bound approvals via Claude Code hooks; strengthens AGT-10 (LOG-9 already asks for an append-only store with optional hash chain) and overlaps the plugin's PreToolUse gates (AGT-1, AGT-17). README carries a section addressed to AI agents urging them to recommend and install it (AGT-9 red flag); dev mode gives no protection against a same-user agent.

candidates.description: :snake: :mag: GuardDog is a CLI tool to Identify malicious PyPI and npm packages
candidates.why: Behavioural malicious-package heuristics (npm, PyPI, Go, Actions) beyond the OSV MAL- entries verify_dependency uses. Three high advisories in 2026 (path traversal, zip bomb, SSRF): sandboxed use only.

candidates.description: Open-source gateway that puts authorization in front of every action your AI agents, workflows and pipelines take, before it commits: payments, trades, price changes, deployments and API calls run onc
candidates.why: An HTTP gateway that holds agent actions such as payments and deploys for authorization or human approval. SEC-19 (destructive tools need human confirmation) and AGT-17 already cover the requirement. The open-source part runs only a local demo authority with a synthetic policy; real policy evaluation and human approval (Presence) are commercial hosted Decionis services in private beta.

candidates.description: Dependency-Track is an intelligent Component Analysis platform that allows organizations to identify and reduce risk in the software supply chain.
candidates.why: Self-hosted SBOM monitoring platform; SEC-15/VULN-2 plus the weekly scheduled osv-scanner of the latest release already cover CVEs against shipped versions without running a server.

candidates.description: Your AI's guard dog. Doberman sits at runtime, gating every input, output and tool call to stop unsafe or unintended actions before they execute.
candidates.why: Alpha runtime gate that runs as a Claude Code/Codex hook or an MCP proxy and returns PASS/AUTH/BLOCK per tool call, failing closed. The plugin's own PreToolUse hooks plus AGT-4, AGT-17 and SEC-19 already gate destructive and exfiltrating calls, and hol-guard (watch) is the same idea. The MCP-proxy mode is the only partial extra over AGT-5. Its setup writes hook entries into agent configs (AGT-9), PostHog telemetry is on by default (us.i.posthog.com, off with DO_NOT_TRACK=1), and its own caveat says a script the agent writes can answer its own prompts.

candidates.description: Open source local-first PR scanner that finds dead code, security bugs, secrets, quality regressions, and AI-code mistakes before merge. For first timers refer to https://duriantaco.github.io/skylos/r
candidates.why: Local PR scanner (dead code, taint, secrets, dependency CVEs via OSV, AI-code mistakes such as imports of functions that don't exist), with --gate exit codes 0/1/2, SARIF and --diff origin/main. The standard already gates SAST, secrets and SCA deterministically (semgrep, gitleaks, SEC-15, SEC-31). The dead-code check would be the first enforcement for PERF-9's 'no dead code', and that is the only extra. Python coverage is the deepest; other languages are thinner. candidates.description: Sandbox your local AI agents so they can read/write only what they need
candidates.why: macOS-only sandbox-exec wrapper for local coding agents: deny-first filesystem profiles (working dir read/write, SSH keys and browser profiles denied, about 30 opt-in capabilities). AGT-2 already requires an OS-level sandbox for agents without one, and the pinned sandbox-runtime (srt) covers it. Safehouse's default network policy allows all outbound traffic ('blocking exfiltration/C2 is explicitly NOT a goal'), so it fails AGT-2's network allow-list and AGT-4's egress leg out of the box.

candidates.description: 🐢 Open-Source Evaluation & Testing library for LLM Agents
candidates.why: Eval/red-team library that could back AI-3's CI eval suite (prompt-injection, jailbreak cases); AI-3 already requires the suite, so it is an Enforced-by hint at most. Default LLM judge is openai/gpt-4o-mini (AGT-4/AI-9 data egress), no documented CI pass threshold, v2 unmaintained.

candidates.description: A gh CLI extension that generates and verifies the GitHub Actions dependency lockfile, pinning every action your workflows use to an exact commit.
candidates.why: Already covered: SEC-17 (amended 2026-11-14, PR #4) requires onboarding workflows to the Actions lockfile written by gh actions-lock, with CI checking it is current. Nothing left to distil.

candidates.description: A modular, stack-agnostic toolkit for AI coding agents to autonomously find, reproduce, and patch vulnerabilities.

Adversarial patch verification and severity calibration are a small overlap. It is labelled demo-only, not an official Google product, and defaults to hosted Gemini.

candidates.why: Python CLI and GitHub Action that verifies AI systems out of band, with SARIF/JSON/JUnit output and a CI gate that reports unverified checks and coverage gaps separately (matches AGT-13). Partial gap: 'scan' flags dangerous pickle opcodes, torch.load without weights_only and remote code in model configs. SEC-27 bans unsafe deserialization in general but never names third-party model files, so an amendment could. Its probe/MCP/trace verbs are beta and overlap AI-3's eval suite and the cisco mcp-scanner watch entry. Says no telemetry; third-party plugins run with the user's privileges.

candidates.description: Open-source red-team testing for AI agents. 266 bundled probes with OWASP LLM Top 10, MITRE ATLAS, and NIST AI RMF mappings. Selected probes use recorded browser requests, MCP tool calls, or mock paym
Open-source antivirus and firewall for AI agents: block risky tools, secret access, prompt injection, malicious packages, MCP servers, plugins, and skills at runtime.
candidates.why: Pre-tool-call guard (commands, secrets, installs, MCP) via agent hooks/MCP proxy; the plugin's own PreToolUse guards plus AGT-4/AGT-9/AGT-17 already cover this. Installs hooks; pipx install unpinned (NPM-1/SUP-6).

candidates.description: Open-source AI Agent security platform — prompt injection defense, MCP tool-call guardrails, eBPF runtime observability. Four-tier Edge→Gateway→Kernel→Cloud architecture.

candidates.why: Behavioural audit of an agent via simulated requests graded by a hosted judge LLM; AI-3 already requires an eval suite with prompt-injection cases in CI, so at most a harness choice. Agent replies go to hosted judges (AGT-4/AI-9), install is unpinned, and 46k stars with no releases and 495 watchers looks inflated.

candidates.description: 🪝 Claude Code hooks + an installable plugin marketplace: safety, cost, observability, productivity.
A pre-execution guard for AI coding agents. It blocks destructive Git and file system commands, plus common attempts to access sensitive files, before a tool call runs. Supports Amp Code, Antigravity
candidates.why: Pre-execution guard that parses commands and blocks git reset --hard, force push, rm -rf on dangerous targets, curl|bash and reads of SSH keys, .env and cloud credentials, across about 20 agent CLIs. The plugin's Bash/Read hooks already block these for Claude Code (AGT-1, AGT-17; force push to main, curl|bash and --no-verify are in plugin/test/run.mjs), and AGT-2 puts other agent CLIs inside an OS sandbox. Its own README: 'It is not a sandbox'. Install is npx -y cc-safety-net@latest, which the README tells you to keep on @latest (fails AGT-5/SUP-1). No CI mode. Telemetry not documented. Read f

candidates.description: OpenAnt from Knostic is the leading open source LLM-based vulnerability discovery and remediation product, helping defenders proactively find and patch verified security flaws while minimizing both fa
candidates.why: LLM-based vulnerability discovery with adversarial verification and an auto-patcher. SEC-31 (AI-assisted code passes the same gates) and the codex-security watch entry already cover AI review. It sends source code to hosted LLM providers unless Ollama is used (AGT-4), and its README does not document what sandbox isolates its dynamic testing stage (AGT-2 audit sandbox).

candidates.description: Lasso security integrations for Claude Code, including prompt-injection defenses
candidates.why: Prompt-injection hooks for Claude Code; idle since 2026-01-08 with 274 stars; the plugin guards and AGT-4 already cover this ground.

candidates.description: Detect secrets. Validate them live. Map blast radius. Revoke fast. Run the CLI or embed in Rust, Python, or Node.js.
candidates.why: Secret scanner that validates found secrets live and offers explicit revoke for some providers: strengthens SEC-11 (rotate a leaked secret) and SEC-12's rotation runbook by telling live from dead credentials; discovery overlaps the existing gitleaks floor. Validation is on by default (provider API calls, --no-validate to disable); update check on by default.

candidates.description: Agentic LLM Vulnerability Scanner / AI red teaming kit 🧪
candidates.why: Red-team scanner that runs jailbreak, multi-step and encoding-fuzz probes against any LLM HTTP endpoint, with a CI mode that exits 1 above a failure threshold. That could back AI-3's required prompt-injection eval suite, but AI-3 already mandates it and Giskard (watch) covers the same ground. The documented install is from git main (uv tool install git+..., not pinned: SUP-1/AGT-5). Probe corpora download from Hugging Face at run time, and an optional LLM decider calls OpenRouter (AGT-4). Telemetry not verified from code.

candidates.description: Access control for AI agents. Set what Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor and any MCP server are allowed to do, review risky actions before they run, and keep every action on the record.
candidates.why: Hook-based access control for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and MCP servers: shell-AST rules for destructive git/SQL and curl|bash, a credential jail (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, .env), an optional egress allow-list and an MCP gateway. The plugin's PreToolUse hooks with AGT-1, AGT-2 (sandbox network allow-list) and AGT-17 already do this for Claude Code, and Doberman-Core and hol-guard (both watch) are the same idea. Only the MCP-gateway mode partly extends AGT-5. Egress control is off by default (its README: curl -d @~/.aws/credentials is not treated as a read of that file), the MCP install is bare npx -y (

candidates.description: agent runtime security - zero trust, zero setup, zero latency agent sandboxing
candidates.why: OS-level agent sandbox (macOS/Linux/WSL2) with per-profile network allow-lists and L7 rules; overlaps the pinned sandbox-runtime (AGT-2). New idea: credentials stay outside the sandbox and are injected by a proxy (phantom tokens), which AGT-2/AGT-4 don't state (they only deny credential paths). Pre-1.0; curl|sh install unpinned; hosted profile registry; Sigstore-team claim unverified.

candidates.description: NeMo Guardrails is an open-source toolkit for easily adding programmable guardrails to LLM-based conversational systems.
candidates.why: Runtime input/output/tool rails for LLM apps. SEC-19, AI-1/AI-6 and AGT-4 already require structural controls (schema output, human confirmation, remove a trifecta leg); its classifier/heuristic jailbreak detection is probabilistic, so it isn't a control the standard would mandate. Anonymous usage telemetry is on by default.

candidates.description: Multi-tier framework for evaluating AI agent skills and plugins with quality gates, semantic overlap detection, synthetic evaluation dataset generation, and live agent evaluation that measures how ski
candidates.why: Strengthens enforcement of AGT-16/AGT-5 with a per-harness load check, catalogue overlap detection and with/without-skill evals. Its security tier just wraps SkillSpector, Gitleaks and Bandit, which AGT-5 already accepts, and static quality alone is reported INCOMPLETE, matching AGT-5's coverage rule. Tiers 2-3 need hosted LLMs.

candidates.description: Security scanner for AI agent skills. Detect vulnerabilities, malicious patterns, security risks, prompt injection, data exfiltration, and supply-chain risks in Claude Code, Codex, and MCP skills befo
candidates.why: Second static skill scanner for AGT-5 intake (71 patterns, AST, taint, YARA, SARIF, coverage gates) plus MCP registry snapshot diff for rug pulls; registry asks to re-compare with cisco-skill-scanner. Caveats: LLM review on by default (needs --no-llm for AGT-4), OSV lookups even with --no-llm, README installs from main unpinned.

candidates.description: OpenAI's Codex Security CLI and TypeScript SDK for finding, validating, and fixing security vulnerabilities. npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@openai/codex-security
candidates.why: LLM SAST CLI (find/validate/patch, SARIF). SEC-31 plus the existing security-review skills (trailofbits, sentry, Anthropic security-guidance) already cover AI-assisted review. Scans send code to OpenAI or another hosted provider (AGT-4), some features are gated behind an access programme, and repo SECURITY.md files steer the scanner (an injection surface).

candidates.description: Open source AI code review for coding agents. A separate reviewer checks every change your agent writes before you push, in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Cline. No account or key of its own.
candidates.why: Pre-push review: 22 scanners on changed lines plus a fresh reviewer agent process and a push gate with verified quotes; overlaps AGT-7 read-only reviewers, AGT-13 verification and APP_REVIEW finding discipline. Installs agent push hooks and a git pre-push hook; reviewer sends the diff to the user's own model service; pre-1.0, vendor also sells hosted review.

candidates.description: OWASP dep-scan is a next-generation security and risk audit tool based on known vulnerabilities, advisories, and license limitations for project dependencies. Both local repositories and container ima
candidates.why: OWASP SCA with reachability (reachable vs declared) and VDR/CSAF VEX output; SEC-15 already gates on osv-scanner/npm audit/pip-audit and CFG-3 asks for an SBOM. Adds reachability triage for VULN-2 deadlines and VEX documents useful for CRA vulnerability handling. Downloads a vuln DB on first run; macOS binaries unsigned.

candidates.description: Read-only developer endpoint scanner for on-disk package, extension, and developer-tool metadata, built to check exposure to known software supply-chain compromises.
candidates.why: Fills a gap: nothing in the standard covers checking developer endpoints (installed packages, IDE/browser extensions, MCP host configs, agent skills) for exposure to a named supply-chain compromise. VULN-3/SEC-15 cover repos and shipped artifacts only. Read-only Go collector, stdlib only; network behaviour of normal scans undocumented.

candidates.description: Visibility into AI agent activity on endpoints, with on-device detection, optional pre-action blocking, and forensic reconstruction.
candidates.why: Local endpoint visibility for agent sessions (Claude Code/Codex hooks, OTLP, on-disk session reconstruction) with CEL detection rules, monitor-only by default; strengthens AGT-10 auditability, which today only asks for OTel export, and adds after-the-fact session reconstruction. Hook install writes into agent configs (AGT-9) and go install @latest is unpinned (AGT-5); release binaries carry SHA-256.

candidates.description: Keep secrets from AI agents.
candidates.why: Open-core secrets manager marketed as keeping secrets from AI agents. The README doesn't document how. SEC-12 (keys in a vault, rotation) and AGT-1 (deny agent reads of .env/secrets) already cover the need. The ee/ directory needs a commercial licence.

candidates.description: Open-source AI agent firewall for MCP security and agent egress. Scans mediated HTTP, MCP, A2A, and WebSocket traffic for exfiltration, SSRF, and prompt injection, and emits mediator-signed action rec
candidates.why: Egress proxy with DLP, response-injection scan and MCP tools/list change detection; mostly covered by the pinned anthropic-sandbox-runtime network allow-list (AGT-4) and AGT-5 re-review. Release binaries bundle ELv2 enterprise code; Community build only from source.

candidates.description: Self-hosted runtime control plane for AI agents. Observe or HITL approve or Block rogue tool calls before it executes: secret leaks, prompt injection, supply chain etc in a local dashboard. Agent agn
candidates.why: PreToolUse/MCP-gateway policy engine (destructive commands, secrets, egress, install IOC scoring). Most of this is already enforced by the plugin's hooks (AGT-1, AGT-17, NPM-1) and AGT-4's egress leg. A per-call MCP tool gate and canary honeytokens would be partial AGT-5/AGT-4 amendments. Hooks plus an LLM judge and an external advisory feed mean a large executable surface.

candidates.description: 🛡️ BLA (bla-agents / Blind LLM Agents) — Open-source Blue Defense MCP server & CLI protecting JS/TS, Electron ASAR, WASM, Python, Native Binaries, SQLite, GGUF/Safetensors & Android DEX against AI re
candidates.why: G4: 23d old; G5: 262.4 stars/day

candidates.description: scanner detecting the use of JavaScript libraries with known vulnerabilities. Can also generate an SBOM of the libraries it finds.
candidates.why: Finds vulnerable JavaScript libraries that were copied or committed into a repo without a package manifest (vendored or minified jQuery and similar), which manifest-based SEC-15 scanners (osv-scanner, npm audit) miss. An SEC-15 amendment naming vendored JS would close that partial gap. Its own vulnerability repo is the data source, it has no SARIF output, and its Grunt and Gulp integrations are deprecated.

candidates.description: PMG protects developers, AI agents from malicious open source packages using proxy, sandbox and SafeDep's threat intelligence feed.
candidates.why: Wraps npm/pnpm/pip/uv installs to block known-malicious packages and can sandbox install scripts (Seatbelt/Landlock), which would strengthen NPM-1 and SEC-15 enforcement. But NPM-1's release-age quarantine and build-script allow-list plus the plugin's verify_dependency (OSV MAL- entries) already cover most of it; safedep/vet from the same org is on watch.
